fault: The whole keyboard backlight is dead, with no lighting on any key.
diagnosis: A dead backlight on every key usually means a cable, port or lighting-mode problem, not a bad switch. We will unplug, check the cable and port, check the mode switch, then plug back in and test.
safety_notes: Unplug the USB-C cable before touching the port or blowing air into the keyboard.
Touch grounded metal first to discharge static before handling the board.

steps.title: Unplug the keyboard
steps.instruction: Pull the USB-C cable out of the back of the keyboard. Touch grounded metal first to discharge static.
steps.expected_visual_state: No cable is plugged into the keyboard's USB-C port and the backlight is off.
common_mistakes: Reaching for the board without grounding yourself first.
Leaving the cable plugged in while working on the board.

steps.title: Check the USB-C port
steps.instruction: Look into the USB-C port on the back of the keyboard. Blow out any dust with compressed air.
steps.expected_visual_state: The USB-C port is open, clean and free of lint or debris, with the connector tongue visible inside.
common_mistakes: Poking metal objects into the port.
Not noticing a bent or loose port.

steps.title: Check the mode switch
steps.instruction: Find the mode switch and set it to the wired (cable) position.
steps.expected_visual_state: The mode switch is slid fully to the wired position, not halfway between positions.
common_mistakes: Leaving the switch in a wireless position.
Leaving the switch stuck halfway between positions.

steps.title: Plug in and test the backlight
steps.instruction: Plug the USB-C cable firmly into the keyboard, then press the key three times to test. Watch whether the backlight comes on.
steps.expected_visual_state: The cable is plugged into the USB-C port and the backlight glows under the keys.
common_mistakes: Not pushing the cable in all the way.
Using a charge-only or damaged cable.
